about: A file of a file data source as one table, through Clarity.Formats (docs/FORMATS-PLAN.md, "A file as a data source"): `read_table` gives, for a flat file (CSV), the file's columns in its order and its rows; for a file that nests (JSON, YAML, XML; see formats-xml-table.json), a first column `#node` holding each record's node as its format writes one (an object's JSON), so what no column maps stays in place, then one column per mapped field, in the order given; the cells of the columns the entity maps (`fields`, matched as names are) are fitted as SQLite keeps the stack's values (a yes or no as 1 or 0; a decimal, a date or a list of values as text), the others kept as the file has them; an empty field or a missing name is null. `write_table` writes a table back: for CSV the whole file, for JSON and YAML the list at `at` inside `original`, the rest kept (YAML keeps the file as written outside what changed: comments, quoting, spacing, an unchanged record as written), each row's record from its `#node` (a new one when null) with its mapped columns set (null removes the member); mapped columns turned back (1 as true). Each runtime keeps the table in an in-memory SQLite database while the program runs, writing the file back after each change. Cells are JSON values: a whole number as a number, a decimal as its text. An empty file (a new one, which a runtime reads as empty when it is not there yet) is the entity's columns without rows; writing it back makes the file, for JSON with the list inside the objects `at` names.

read.name: a CSV's columns in its order, mapped ones fitted as SQLite keeps them (true as 1), the others kept as text, empty as null
another separator; without a header the columns are the entity's
a JSON list at a path: each record's node kept whole in '#node' (a record inside stays there), then the mapped columns
a YAML list at a path, as JSON's: each record's node kept whole in '#node' as its JSON, then the mapped columns
read.input:
# logins
data:
  - site: a
    visits: 3
    owner: {n: 1}
  - site: b   # no visits
    extra: true
next: ~

read.name: a column the entity maps that the file lacks
a value that does not fit says its row and column
read.error: row 2: column 'visits' is an integer, not "many"

read.name: an empty file, a new one not written yet, is the entity's columns without rows

write.name: CSV written whole: the file's columns in its order, 1 as true, null as empty, quoted where needed

JSON: the list at the path replaced, the rest of the file kept; each record from its node with what no column maps (a record inside) in place; numbers and yes or no as JSON has them; null leaves a member out
a new JSON file gets the list inside the objects its path names

YAML written back keeps the file as written outside what changed: comments, quoting and spacing; an unchanged record as written, a changed one rewritten where it changed with what no column maps kept, a new one in block style
write.original:
# Logins, kept by hand
data:
  # the first one
  - site: a      # main
    visits: 3
    owner: {n: 1}
  - site: 'b'
    visits: 5
    note: keep me
next: ~   # nothing yet
write.written:
# Logins, kept by hand
data:
  # the first one
  - site: a      # main
    visits: 3
    owner: {n: 1}
  - site: 'b'
    visits: 6
    note: keep me
  - site: c
    visits: 1
next: ~   # nothing yet

write.name: a YAML record deleted takes the comments before it along; the rest stays as written
write.original:
# Logins, kept by hand
data:
  # the first one
  - site: a      # main
    visits: 3
    owner: {n: 1}
  - site: 'b'
    visits: 5
    note: keep me
next: ~   # nothing yet
write.written:
# Logins, kept by hand
data:
  - site: 'b'
    visits: 5
    note: keep me
next: ~   # nothing yet

write.name: a YAML list written in flow style becomes block style when it changes; values as YAML writes them, null leaving a key out
write.written:
data:
  - site: a
    visits: 3
    owner:
      n: 1
    paid: true
    price: 12.5
  - site: "true"
    paid: false
next: null # stays

write.name: a new YAML file gets the list inside the mappings its path names
a new CSV file gets its header row
